groups.title: Cooling
groups.summary: AC repair, installation, replacement and maintenance for systems that run most of the year.
groups.intro: Air conditioning systems in Houston run for extended hours, which makes correct sizing, airflow and component condition the things that decide whether a system lasts. Cooling work here covers diagnosis, repair, replacement and seasonal maintenance, with a written quote before anything is started. One thing worth knowing: the expensive-sounding symptom is not always the expensive repair, and every summer homeowners call panicking about a dead compressor when the real problem is a capacitor or a contactor.

groups.title: Air Quality & Systems
groups.summary: Testing, filtration, purification, ventilation and humidity control for the air the system is actually moving.
groups.intro: A system can hold temperature and still be moving air you would rather not breathe. Indoor air work covers testing first, then the filtration, purification, ventilation and humidity control that the test result actually calls for. Filters are the starting point: a clogged filter is one of the most common causes of AC failure in Houston homes, because restricted airflow freezes the evaporator coil and shuts the system down.

about.title: Your locally operated heating and cooling company since 2016
text: 75 Degree AC was founded in 2016 with a clear mission: to deliver reliable, efficient, high-quality HVAC work for homeowners and businesses across the Houston, TX area. From the start the focus has been on doing the work correctly, communicating clearly, and standing behind every service call.

The company is independently owned and operated out of Houston rather than run as a franchise, so every call, quote and follow-up comes from the local team. Lead technician Kenny Ho handles installations and major repairs personally.

Technicians carry EPA Section 608 universal certification and train on every major brand, including Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, Rheem, Daikin and Mitsubishi. The work covers residential and light-commercial systems: single-family homes, apartments, offices, retail units, restaurants and medical clinics across Greater Houston.
Growth has come from repeat customers and referrals, built on consistent service, honest recommendations and accountability for the work performed.

faqs.q: How much does an HVAC service call cost in Houston?
faqs.a: The standard diagnostic fee is $89, and that fee is waived when you approve the recommended repair. Replacement estimates are free. Repair pricing depends on the failed part, the system type, the age of the equipment, how accessible it is, and whether the issue is isolated or tied to a larger performance problem. A capacitor replacement is a very different call from a blower motor failure or a refrigerant leak.

faqs.q: Why is my AC running but not cooling my home?
faqs.a: In Houston, long run times put extra stress on air conditioning systems. Common causes are airflow restrictions, low refrigerant, dirty coils, or electrical components struggling under heat load. A proper system diagnostic identifies the real issue before it turns into a larger failure.

faqs.q: Do you offer same-day AC repair in Houston?
faqs.a: Calls received before 2 PM Monday to Saturday are dispatched the same day across Houston and the surrounding area. Response time depends on call volume and system condition, but urgent cooling issues are prioritized whenever possible, and emergency service is available 24/7.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need AC repair or a full replacement?
faqs.a: If the system still cools but struggles to keep up, cycles frequently, or needs repeated repairs, repair may still make sense. Replacement becomes the better option when cooling is inconsistent, repairs are frequent, or the system cannot handle Houston's summer demand. As a rule, a system over 10 to 15 years old whose repair cost exceeds half the value of a new one is usually better replaced.

faqs.q: What causes uneven cooling in Houston homes?
faqs.a: Uneven temperatures are common here and are usually linked to ductwork issues, airflow imbalance, insulation gaps or system sizing. Even a working AC system struggles if air distribution is uneven, so addressing airflow often improves comfort quickly.

faqs.q: What size AC unit do I need for my home?
faqs.a: Sizing depends on square footage, insulation quality, ceiling height, the number of windows and Houston's specific climate conditions. An oversized unit cycles on and off too often and leaves humidity behind; an undersized one runs constantly without cooling effectively. A detailed load calculation settles it before anything is recommended.

faqs.q: Which AC brands do you install?
faqs.a: Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, Rheem, American Standard, Daikin and Mitsubishi, among others. Each offers different features and price points, and the recommendation is made against your home and budget rather than against a brand quota.

faqs.q: How long does a new AC installation take?
faqs.a: Most residential system replacements take between four and eight hours. New construction or more complex installations can take one to two days. The old equipment is removed, the new system installed, every component tested, and operation verified before anyone leaves.

faqs.q: Is there financing available for a new system?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with several lenders to offer payment plans with a range of rates and terms. Ask about current financing options when you call.

faqs.q: Can a dirty air filter really stop my AC working?
faqs.a: Yes. A clogged filter is one of the most common causes of AC failure in Houston homes. Restricted airflow makes the system work harder, which can freeze the evaporator coil and shut the system down. Filters are best changed every one to three months, especially through the long cooling season.

faqs.q: How often should I schedule HVAC maintenance?
faqs.a: Twice a year: once in spring before the cooling season and once in fall before heating season. Houston systems run longer than in most regions, so routine maintenance reduces breakdowns, improves airflow, and lets small problems be corrected before extreme heat exposes them.

faqs.q: What is included in a tune-up?
faqs.a: Cleaning or replacing air filters, inspecting and cleaning coils, checking refrigerant levels, testing thermostat calibration, lubricating moving parts, tightening electrical connections, inspecting ductwork for leaks, measuring airflow and testing system performance.
